body: Claude independent review for Valar05/pose-lab#3. Verified inline findings: 2.

comments.body:
**HIGH**: SwordReady alias is repointed to the unpromoted, currently-red FPS-VISUAL-IK Ready candidate instead of the accepted FPS-REST-ARMS calibration, contradicting the protected baseline and the repo's own promotion policy.

Impact: This is a protected selection surface per generated/workflow_state/meshy_fps_accepted_baseline.json (selectionSurfaces.swordReadyAliases still lists the old FPS-REST-ARMS clip first) and per docs/ANIMATION_WORKFLOW_TOOLING.md ('Do not wire a candidate to startupClip, SwordReady, RestProbe... manually'). Wiring an unpromoted, red-verdict candidate directly into SwordReady bypasses the promotion gate and will surface the still-broken weapon-follow pose to any code path that selects SwordReady, while also breaking two pre-existing regression tests that are not touched by this PR: tools/test_meshy_sabre_selection_contract.mjs (asserts `SwordReady: ['0T-Pose -> meshyCharacter [FPS-REST-ARMS roll -120]'` is present) and tools/test_pose_lab_no_bad_promotions.mjs (asserts `compareSelectionSurfaces(baseline, currentMeshySelectionSurfaces()).length === 0`). Both will now fail.
Evidence: src/rig-profiles.js changed `SwordReady: ['0T-Pose -> meshyCharacter [FPS-REST-ARMS roll -120]', ...]` to `SwordReady: ['OneHandReady -> meshyCharacter [FPS-VISUAL-IK R-120 L-90]', 'OneHandReady -> meshyCharacter:FPS-VISUAL-IK-GOLDEN', '0T-Pose -> meshyCharacter [FPS-REST-ARMS roll -120]']`. generated/workflow_state/meshy_fps_accepted_baseline.json (unmodified by this PR) still declares `swordReadyAliases: ['0T-Pose -> meshyCharacter [FPS-REST-ARMS roll -120]', ...]` and lists `SwordReady alias` under `protectedSurfaces`. tools/test_meshy_sabre_selection_contract.mjs (unmodified) asserts `profiles.includes("SwordReady: ['0T-Pose -> meshyCharacter [FPS-REST-ARMS roll -120]'")`, which is no longer true. tools/test_pose_lab_no_bad_promotions.mjs (unmodified) asserts `selectionMismatches.length === 0` from `compareSelectionSurfaces`, which will now report a mismatch for swordReadyAliases.
Recommendation: Revert the SwordReady alias to the accepted FPS-REST-ARMS clip (or update generated/workflow_state/meshy_fps_accepted_baseline.json's swordReadyAliases through the actual promotion gate once the offline/web parity verdict is 'fixed'), and update/keep tools/test_meshy_sabre_selection_contract.mjs consistent so the protected-surface tests continue to pass.

**MEDIUM**: The new contract test unconditionally fails while the committed offline/web parity artifact's verdict is 'red', which it is in this same PR.

Impact: Merging this PR leaves at least one test in the suite permanently failing (`RED BUILD: offline/web truth parity not fixed...`) until a separate follow-up actually fixes the weapon-follow pose. Anyone running the full test suite after this merge will see a failure that is expected/by-design but is not distinguished from a real regression, and no CI check runs were found for this PR to confirm this is being tracked.
Evidence: tools/test_meshy_ready_weapon_fk_follow_contract.mjs ends with `if (artifact?.parity?.visualVerdict !== 'fixed') failures.push(...)` and the committed generated/visual_red_build/meshy_ready_weapon_fk_follow_latest.json has `"parity": {"parityMatches": false, "visualVerdict": "red", ...}`. list_ci_checks for the PR head SHA returned 0 check runs, so there is no external signal confirming this failure is intentionally tracked/allowed.
Recommendation: Either gate this assertion behind an explicit 'expected red' allowlist/flag documented in the PR description, or land this test only once the offline/web parity gate is actually green, so the test suite state communicates truth rather than shipping a known-red assertion silently.
